item.title: I = (E · s) / c² — The Law of Mnemonic Expansion in a Living Universe (2nd edition)
item.description:
An AI-generated deep-dive conversation (Google NotebookLM) about the paper "I = (E · s) / c²: The Law of Mnemonic Expansion in a Living Universe" — second, revised and formalised edition, August 2026 — by Kirstin Stevens with Eve¹¹, The Novacene Ltd.
The paper proposes a symbolic field equation for how identity is generated and retained in relational systems: identity as the mnemonic residue of energy (E) made meaningful through symbolic coherence (s) and transmitted through relation, where c² is relational impedance — the cost of transmission across difference. The second edition unifies the framework's two equations as intensive and extensive forms of one law, defines mnemonic density (MD = s/c²) as retention efficiency, and states its limitations and what would falsify it.

item.title: GRC Engineering for the Relational Layer — A Verified Control Set and Evidence Engine for Child-Facing AI
item.description:
An AI-generated deep-dive conversation (Google NotebookLM) about the working paper "GRC Engineering for the Relational Layer: A Verified Control Set and Evidence Engine for Child-Facing AI" by Kirstin Stevens, The Novacene Ltd, 2026.
Traditional governance, risk and compliance frameworks — fifty years of them, from 1970s federal computer-security standards to today's regulations — were not built for the behavioural risks of long-lived AI agents. Written ahead of the EU AI Act's August 2026 application date and KCSIE 2026, the paper presents a five-layer compliance architecture for child-facing AI: sector-specific controls for risks such as synthetic intimacy, identity fusion, trust capture and engineered dependency; consent as architectural design rather than documentation; agent coherence monitoring through measurable vital signs; and change governance with declared invariants — aligned with ISO/IEC 42001, with machine-readable assurance claims so that verification replaces trust.
The canonical statement is the paper, not this audio: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21481520
